= Cytoville repository rulesets
// SPDX-License-Identifier: CC-BY-SA-4.0

GitHub does not apply JSON files in this directory automatically. The live API
is authoritative; these payloads describe the intended rules.

On 2026-11-06 the following zero-bypass protections were created and verified
for Cytoville through the repository Rulesets API:

[cols="2,1,3",options="header"]
|===
|Rule |Live ID |Scope
|Branch-Floor |26719476 |Default branch: prohibit deletion and non-fast-forward updates
|Require-Signed-Commits |26719478 |Default branch: require verified signatures
|Require-Linear-History |26719480 |Default branch: require linear history
|Immutable-Tags |26719481 |All tags: prohibit deletion, updates and force updates; require signatures
|===

Repository merge settings allow squash merges only. The implementation was
consolidated into GitHub-signed commits on top of the verified template pin;
`migration-working-history` preserves the development history. The protections
were enabled after that consolidation.

`base.json` supplies the canonical pull-request policy. Additional live
rulesets, including Base, must be inspected through the API rather than inferred
from a checked-in payload:

[source,bash]
----
gh api repos/catachresis-colloquium/cytoville/rulesets
----

The organisation's separate Actions allowlist blocks the external reusable
Creusot workflow and three inherited support workflows. Branch protection
does not resolve that organisation policy, and no organisation access policy
was changed. See `docs/verification/RECEIPT.adoc` for the validation boundary.
Base uses no bypass actors. The template's application IDs are not installed
in this organisation, so GitHub rejected that inherited bypass list. All
contributors follow the same pull-request policy here.
